<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via loadMany (symbol, a method of class MetadataManager), loadManyKeyed (symbol, a method of class DatabaseLoader))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via loadMany (symbol, a method of class MetadataManager))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json af27439e571a58df54466af7e723307d04fc30a5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `55a27ed3909a24946eaf4b3b1ee62ca8ac6e6684` — the merge of head `99a823e7d015f627dadbb326aa7df167758c6294` into base `af27439e571a58df54466af7e723307d04fc30a5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 55a27ed3909a24946eaf4b3b1ee62ca8ac6e6684 && git checkout 55a27ed3909a24946eaf4b3b1ee62ca8ac6e6684
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin af27439e571a58df54466af7e723307d04fc30a5 99a823e7d015f627dadbb326aa7df167758c6294 && git checkout -B drift-repro af27439e571a58df54466af7e723307d04fc30a5 && git merge --no-ff 99a823e7d015f627dadbb326aa7df167758c6294

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json af27439e571a58df54466af7e723307d04fc30a5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs af27439e571a58df54466af7e723307d04fc30a5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Epic red-line read at `2dd2ecfe` · 2026-11-12T04:23Z

Head-sha: `2dd2ecfeb3cb87bc99812bb597b5d7423a7d0c14`

Base: merge-base `e06d04f945`. Read: the full diff (4 files, +147/−4), the changeset, and the four new pins. Static read; nothing was run.

**PASS on the three red lines.**

- **Red line 1 (resolution never loosened).** Every move narrows or corrects an attribution:
  - A by-package read naming a package that holds no row of the name (the host's own `packageId` included) now answers nothing, where it served another package's body.
  - A read naming a holder answers that holder's own body, where it served the row saved last.
  - Nothing new is admitted. The `onlyBoundStampAdded` skip only suppresses a write whose body differs by its own row's stamp.
- **Red line 2 (ambiguity reported, never guessed).** No new pick is introduced. The pre-existing guess, a bare read of a two-holder name answering the row saved last after the boot pass, is declared in the changeset as not changed. It is carried by #32521 (p1 proposed, in this seat's chain right after this PR).
- **Red line 3 (independently releasable).** The change is additive: no schema or row rewrite, and the ADR-0087 `not-required` marker is present. The one-holder bare read still answers the unique holder, now stamped with its package. That move is declared and pinned (`one holder — … a bare read answers the unique holder, now stamped`). Each moved answer is declared FROM → TO under `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and pinned per type over the five unbundled slotted types taken from the tree:
  - stamped `loadMany` with no package-less insert;
  - registered under its own package, never the host's;
  - a stamp-only save writes nothing.

Landing note: this PR and #32544 share `database-loader.ts` and `metadata-manager.ts` with the epic chain's `du44hj` and `phk4r9`, so trial-merge before queueing.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2dd2ecfeb3cb87bc99812bb597b5d7423a7d0c14`
Local-runs: none
Scope: (no `hits` — narrowing face, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`) + packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts

Read, not reviewed: `package-slotted-store.ts`, `loaders/filesystem-loader.ts`, `loaders/memory-loader.ts`, `loaders/loader-interface.ts`, `plugin.ts` (`_loadFromFileSystem`), `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` (the `loadMany` / `loadManyKeyed` consumers), `packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts`. The test file and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on this head at review time. Concluded, all success: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Plan Test Core shards, Test UI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label, filter. None failed. **Still running, so not covered by this verdict:** Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI. The rest are skipped. A red among the pending ones overrides this record.

### ① Derived judgments

Each moved answer the diff implies, checked against the tree at the head:

1. `MetadataManager.get(type, name, P)` after the boot pass, P holding no row of the name: another package's body → nothing. **Right**, and it is the one narrowing. The boot pass now registers the stamped body under the row's own slot (`applyProtection` is a no-op on a stamped item, so a host `packageId` no longer claims it).
2. Same read, P holding a row: the last-saved row's body → P's own. **Right** (correction; the read falls through to the loader's slots).
3. `MetadataManager.loadMany` hands a column-bound row on stamped `_packageId`. **Right.** `withEntryPackage` stamps only a body that names no package, so a legacy row's hand-out copy keeps its identity for `bindReadRowPackage`.
4. `DatabaseLoader.save` of row body + the row's own stamp writes nothing. **Right.** `onlyBoundStampAdded` requires the target row to be bound to that same package, so a package-less row taken over (`replaces`) is still written and bound.
5. `DatabaseLoader.loadManyKeyed` entries gain `packageId` for the five types. **Right, additive**: `loaderEntries` and `admitKeyedLoaderItems` drop it for an unbundled type, `list()` reads `loadManySlots`, and objectql's keyed action read uses name and data only.
6. **Undeclared, wrong as declared** — see ④ F1: `MetadataManager.loadMany` of the five types now drops a body its loader's keyed read cannot name, over the `FilesystemLoader` as well as the `DatabaseLoader`.

`Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, value or type an author writes moves.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/metadata` is right: kind `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO lines, the one-line fix, one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, sound: no stored row changes) and both declaration lines, identical to the PR body. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the correct arm. `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none.
- Deviation, arm declared `no (narrowing)` where the dispatch expected `no`: correct, the tree narrows (① item 1).
- Deviation, downstream suites run before the `main` merge: answered by the head's own check-runs, of which Test Core and Build Core are still pending (above).
- Out-of-scope F1 of the dev (one row primed per name; the bare read of a two-holder name answers the last-saved row): unchanged by this diff, filed as #32521. Accepted as out of scope.
- Card step 1 asked for the measurement on `main` after #32214; it was taken at `27abd458a8`, #32214's final head. Equivalent; no action.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the spec on `main`: it takes no declared capability away. A read naming a package that holds nothing was served another package's body; ADR-0150 D4 addresses these types per `(package, name)`, so answering nothing makes the store's own rule real. Both implementing files agree with the card's ruling, with one gap.

**F1 — should-fix. `MetadataManager.loadMany` drops nameless bodies for the five types, undeclared, and first-party reach is not 0.**
`metadata-manager.ts` now routes `api`, `agent`, `skill`, `action`, `permission` through `loader.loadManyKeyed` for every loader that has one, not only the `DatabaseLoader`. The keyed read is not the same population as `loadMany`:
- `FilesystemLoader.loadManyKeyed` drops a file with no resolvable name and no body `name` (a nested or extension-less file); `FilesystemLoader.loadMany` returns it. `NodeMetadataManager` wires this loader, so every Node host is on this path.
- `DatabaseLoader.loadManyKeyed` drops a row whose `name` column is not a non-empty string; `readTypeRows`' own jsdoc says such a row "is still a body `loadMany` must return — dropping it would change what consumers see today".

FROM: `MetadataManager.loadMany(type)` returns those bodies. TO: it does not. The PR body and the changeset say only a host that wires a `DatabaseLoader` reaches any moved answer. That sentence is false for this one. No in-tree consumer sees a difference (the boot pass, objectql's action resync and `loadMany`'s own dedupe all skip a nameless body), which is why this is not a must-fix. Fix either way: keep the bodies the keyed read cannot name (append them from `loader.loadMany`), or declare the row FROM → TO in the changeset and PR body and pin it. #32214 made the same move for `email_template`; if it is declared here, say so for both.

**F2 — nit.** The `[#31699 R4-B]` jsdoc on `onlyBoundStampAdded` and on `withEntryPackage` still reads as the bundled-type rule only; the call sites carry the `[#32458]` note. Leave as is or fold into F1's fix.

No must-fix. F1 earns a delta review of its fix.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none
Scope: (no `hits` — narrowing face, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`) + packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts

This is the delta round over the record 6814501208 (head `2dd2ecfe`). It covers that record's findings F1 and F2 and everything `2dd2ecfe..03b71429` changed: three commits, five files. Everything else stands as judged there.

Read, not reviewed: `loaders/filesystem-loader.ts`, `loaders/memory-loader.ts`, `loaders/loader-interface.ts`, `plugin.ts` (`_loadFromFileSystem`), `MetadataManager.register` / `save` / `loadManyKeyed`, `packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts`. The test file, the changeset and the doc page are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the doc sentence and the changeset lines are judged below for agreement with the code only.

Check-runs on this head at review time (50 total, 15 skipped). No red.
- Concluded, all success (14): Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test UI, filter.
- **Still running, so not covered by this verdict (21):** Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI.

A red among the pending ones is a FAIL of the gate and overrides this record. The new pin runs in Test Core, so it has no CI verdict yet.

### ① Derived judgments

What the head move changes, against `main`:

1. **F1 is closed under ruling (a).** For `api`, `agent`, `skill`, `action`, `permission`, `MetadataManager.loadMany` again takes its bodies from `loader.loadMany`, so every body is kept, in the loader's order. `FilesystemLoader` has no `loadManySlots`, so `withLoaderEntryPackages` returns its items untouched: its answer is `main`'s. A `DatabaseLoader` row with an empty `name` column is returned, unstamped. **Right.**
2. The bundled path (`email_template`) is back to `main`'s condition, character for character. **Right, no move.**
3. `MemoryLoader` has both methods, but its keyed entries carry no `packageId` for these types, so nothing is stamped. **Right, no move.** The changeset's "only `DatabaseLoader` answers a package there" is true.
4. A column-bound `DatabaseLoader` row whose body names itself is stamped with its row's package, as declared. A legacy row's hand-out copy keeps its identity (`withEntryPackage` returns the same object when the body names a package), so `bindReadRowPackage` still finds it. **Right.**
5. **Undeclared, wrong** — see ④ F3: the stamp is joined on the body's `name` against the keyed entry's key. A body whose `name` is another row's key is stamped with that other row's package.
6. A column-bound row whose body carries no `name` stays unstamped, as on `main`. **Right as code** (no consumer registers a nameless body), but the prose says otherwise: ④ F4.

`Metadata-protocol: none` still holds.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata` with the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, one ADR-0087 marker. Only the first FROM → TO bullet of the changeset changed. It matches the tree for the cases it names, with the F3 and F4 gaps. The other bullets were re-read against the head and still hold. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- F1's ruling, option (a): implemented as ruled (① item 1).
- No new dev flag and no `open_questions` entry arrived with the delta.
- The PR body still describes the first head: ④ F5.

### ④ Design judgment

**F1 — closed.** See ① item 1. The pin is real: `every body loadMany answered is kept…` wires a `FilesystemLoader` and a `DatabaseLoader`, and asserts five bodies per type (a flat file, a nested nameless file, an extension-less file, a row with an empty `name` column, the column-bound row stamped `BETA`). At `2dd2ecfe` the keyed read drops three of the five, so the length and the membership assertions both fail there. Its CI verdict is pending with Test Core.

**F2 — closed.** Both jsdoc blocks now name the unbundled types and point at `withLoaderEntryPackages`.

**F3 — should-fix. `withLoaderEntryPackages` can stamp a body with another row's package.**
The map is keyed by the keyed entry's `name` (the row's `name` column); the lookup uses the body's own `name`. The two are different identities, and this file's own #14205 notes say so. `register` refuses a body whose `name` disagrees with its key, but `MetadataManager.save` and `DatabaseLoader.save` do not, so such a row is storable through a public door.
- Case: row keyed `b`, body `name: 'a'`, bound to BETA or to no package; row keyed `a`, bound to ALPHA.
- FROM (`main`): row `b`'s body is handed on unstamped.
- TO: it is handed on with `_packageId: ALPHA`, a package its row is not bound to. If it comes first, `loadMany`'s by-name dedupe keeps it and drops ALPHA's own body, and the boot pass registers it in ALPHA's slot.
- The first head stamped each entry's own body, so this is new with the delta. It is not declared, and it is a package attributed by guess, which the epic's red line 2 rules out.
- Not a must-fix: it needs a row written past `register`'s contract, first-party reach is 0, and the body served for the name is the one `main` served.
- Fix: stamp only when the entry's own body carries the entry's key as its `name` and exactly one item of `items` carries that name; otherwise leave the body unstamped, as on `main`. Pin the case. Or declare the row FROM → TO and pin it.

**F4 — nit (prose).** The changeset bullet and the new sentence in `metadata-service.mdx` say a row bound by the `package_id` column alone reaches `loadMany` stamped. For the five unbundled types that holds only when the body carries its own `name`; a named row with a nameless body is unstamped (the function's jsdoc says this correctly). The doc sentence sits in the paragraph about nameless bodies, so it is the case a reader there has in mind. The rest of the sentence agrees with the code: `MetadataManager.loadManyKeyed` returns the body as stored, without the stamp.

**F5 — nit (PR body).** "What changes" item 1 still says `loadMany` reads every slotted type through the keyed entries, the change is still called three one-line conditions, and the verify line expects 21 cases. The head has a second read path, a new function and 22 cases.

No must-fix. F3 earns a delta review of its fix. F4 and F5 are prose and can ride with it.

1. **F3 is closed under the seat's ruling.** `withLoaderEntryPackages` now records a package for a key only when that entry's own body carries the key as its `name`, and stamps an item only when exactly one item in the loader's answer carries that `name`. In `DatabaseLoader` both reads come from the same rows (`unscopedTypeRows`), so the one item named `N` is the body of the entry keyed `N`: a stamped body is always its own row's. **Right.**
2. Against `03b71429`, the stamp is only narrowed; no body gains one. A row whose own body names itself, beside another body of the same `name` in the same loader's answer, is now handed on unstamped, as on `main`. The changeset declares it. **Right.**
3. Against `main`, the only move is still the declared one: a column-bound row whose body carries the row's own `name`, alone under that name, is stamped. **Right.**
4. A legacy row's hand-out copy keeps its identity on both paths (returned as is, or by `withEntryPackage` unchanged), so `bindReadRowPackage` still finds it. **Right, no move.**
5. `FilesystemLoader` (no `loadManySlots`) and `MemoryLoader` (no `packageId` on its entries) answer as before. **Right, no move.**
6. In the counter-example, `MetadataManager.loadMany`'s by-name dedupe keeps the first body and drops ALPHA's own. That is `main`'s behavior and, by the seat's ruling, not this PR's to change. Not graded.

`Metadata-protocol: none` still holds.
